About

From an abandoned flax factory to a regional lifeline.

Kisiizi’s roots trace to the East Africa Revival of the 1920s and a waterfall-powered factory built by Italian prisoners of war. When the factory closed after the Second World War, the Church of Uganda saw its chance to bring practical care — and, in 1958, a hospital was born.

Aerial views of the Kisiizi Hospital compound, set into the surrounding hills

28 March 1958

Dr John & Doreen Sharp arrive

They camp in one of the old factory buildings. By the first Monday morning, thirty people are already queuing to be seen.

1959 – 1960

The factory becomes a hospital

An operating theatre, labour ward, sterilising rooms and stores are carved out of the old buildings. By March 1960, two wards with 24 beds are open for in-patients.

1966

Loss, and continuity

Dr Sharp dies of a brain tumour; his successor, Dr Pat Walker, is killed in a car accident soon after. Neither loss — nor the political turmoil of the Amin and Obote years that follows — closes the hospital’s doors.

1989 – 1998

Schools, sponsorship, nursing

The Primary School opens in 1989. Facing a growing AIDS crisis, Kisiizi launches child sponsorship in 1995 and founds its own School of Nursing & Midwifery in 1998.

2008

Golden Jubilee

Fifty years on, Kisiizi marks its Golden Jubilee with the Archbishop of Uganda in attendance — alongside a former patient who by then was the country’s President. The partnership with Countess of Chester Hospital begins the same year.

2026

Approaching seventy years

Kisiizi looks toward its 70th anniversary in 2028, still guided by the same conviction that brought Dr Sharp here: that care should never be turned away.

Staff, students and colleagues mark 65 years of Kisiizi Hospital, 2023.

Medical superintendents, 1958–present

Names with a – open to a short history. The rest are here as record only — if you served at Kisiizi during those years, or knew someone who did, the hospital would welcome hearing from you.

Dr John Sharp1958–1966+
Arrived with his wife Doreen on 28 March 1958 to camp in one of the old flax-factory buildings that became this hospital — a queue of thirty was already waiting to be seen by the following Monday. Son of the missionary doctor Leonard Sharp, who had founded Kabale Hospital and the Lake Bunyonyi leper colony a generation earlier. Led Kisiizi until a brain tumour ended his life in 1966.
Dr Pat Walker1966+
Took over after Dr Sharp’s death and was killed in a car accident not long after — a second devastating loss in quick succession for the young hospital.
Dr Jack Symonds1966–1967
Dr John Davies1967–1977
Dr Kevin Vaughan1977–1986
Dr Amos Twinamasiko1986–1988
Dr Edward Turitwenka1988–1989
Dr Ian Spillman1989–1993+
A consultant paediatrician who first worked at Kisiizi from 1987 with his wife Hanna, a nurse and midwife. On leaving in 1993, the couple spent nineteen years in the UK coordinating Friends of Kisiizi and visiting regularly.
Dr Peter Wood1993–1996
Dr Lionel Mills1996–2000
Dr Peter Winfrey2000–2003
Dr Tonny Tumwesigye2003–2012+
Went on to become Executive Director of the Uganda Protestant Medical Bureau, representing Uganda’s church-run hospitals nationally and internationally.
Dr Ian Spillman2012–2022+
Asked to take up the Medical Superintendent role again in 2012, he and Hanna returned to live at Kisiizi for another decade of service.
Dr Henry Lukabwe2022–present+
Grew up in Mukono, central Uganda, and trained in medicine at Mbarara University of Science and Technology. Did part of his internship at Kisiizi before completing it at Mulago National Referral Hospital, then returned in 2013 as a Medical Officer. Kisiizi went on to sponsor his postgraduate degree in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, completed in 2018, after which he joined the hospital’s management committee. He is married to Ruth, with two children, Hadriel and Henrietta.

A Church of Uganda mission hospital in the Kigezi highlands of Rukungiri District, South-Western Uganda.
